e01: In this little village lived a young woman named Mary, engaged to Joseph.
One day the angel Gabriel came and told her she would have a son.
Mary was silent for a long while, and then she quietly bowed her head.
e02: Joseph came here with Mary, whose time to give birth was near, to be registered.
There was no guest room, so they lay down where the animals stayed — and that night Mary gave birth to her firstborn son.
Shepherds from the fields outside town ran through the dark and found the baby in the manger.
e03: Joseph and Mary carried the baby up to this temple.
Old Simeon, who had lived holding on to God's promise, took the baby in his arms and praised God.
Anna, eighty-four years old, came up too and told everyone who was waiting about this child.
e04: Magi from the east saw a star and traveled a long way to find him.
The star stopped over the place where the child was, and they bowed down and worshiped.
They gave gold, frankincense and myrrh, and then, as a dream warned them, went home another way.
e05: An angel spoke to Joseph in a dream, and he set out that very night.
The family traveled the dry road all the way down to this far southern land and stayed here.
Meanwhile Herod realized the Magi had outwitted him, and he burned with rage.
e06: After Herod died, Joseph's family set out again on the long road from Egypt.
They were afraid to go to Judea, so they settled in this little town up north in Galilee.
I grew up in this hillside village. They were quiet years the world knew nothing about.
e07: The year I turned twelve, I came up here with my parents for the Passover.
When everyone went home, I stayed behind among the teachers, listening and asking questions.
My parents traveled a day, turned back, and after three days found me here.
e08: This riverbank was crowded with people coming to be baptized for repentance.
When I came, John tried hard to stop me, but I went down into this water.
As I came up out of the water and prayed, heaven opened and the Spirit came down like a dove.
e09: After my baptism, the Spirit led me into this land of rock and sand.
When I had eaten nothing for forty days and nights, the tempter came.
Each of the three temptations I answered with the words of Scripture. When the devil left, angels came.
e10: Here John pointed to me as I passed by, and two of his disciples followed me.
It was about four in the afternoon. They spent the rest of that day where I was staying.
Andrew went straight to his brother Simon and told him they had found the Messiah.
e11: My mother was at a wedding feast in this village, and my disciples and I were invited too.
Just as the laughter and songs were at their height, the wine ran out, and the servants' faces froze.
In that house where six stone jars stood, my first sign was revealed.
e12: When I came up for the Passover, this courtyard was lined with animal sellers and money changers.
I made a whip out of cords, drove out the animals and overturned the money tables.
Watching it, my disciples remembered a verse from the Psalms.
e13: Late at night, Nicodemus, a leader of the Pharisees, quietly came to see me.
By the light of one flickering lamp, we sat face to face and talked deep into the night.
The words spoken that night lingered long in the still darkness.
e14: Around noon, tired from the long road, I sat down by this well of Jacob.
A Samaritan woman came to draw water, and I asked her for a drink.
She left her water jar behind and ran back to the town. You rest here a while too.
e15: A royal official from Capernaum came all the way up here, out of breath.
At home his son was dying of a fever.
He believed my word and set off, and on the way down he met his servants — with news that the boy was alive.
e16: On the Sabbath, in the synagogue of the village where I grew up, I unrolled the scroll of Isaiah.
People were amazed, yet they whispered, Isn't this Joseph's son?
Angry people dragged me to the edge of a cliff, but I walked right through the middle of them.
e17: Fishermen who had caught nothing all night were washing their nets by this shore.
I got into Simon's boat and taught the crowd gathered at the water's edge.
That day the fish filled two boats so full they began to sink, and they left everything to follow me.
e18: On the Sabbath, in this village's synagogue, a man with an unclean spirit cried out.
After leaving the synagogue, I took Simon's mother-in-law by the hand and helped her up. The fever left her.
When the sun set, the whole town crowded to the door, bringing the sick.
e19: This house was so packed, right up to the door, that there was no room to stand.
Four men carried a paralyzed man here, opened a hole in the roof and lowered him down on his mat.
I saw their faith. That day he got up in front of everyone and walked out.
e20: At the tax booth by this road sat Matthew, a tax collector people pointed their fingers at.
At one word from me, he got up, left everything and followed me.
At the feast in his house, tax collectors and sinners reclined at the table with us. Laughter spilled out of the house.
e21: At the pool of Bethesda by the Sheep Gate, sick people lay packed in the shade of every porch.
Among them was a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years.
He only complained that there was no one to put him into the pool.
e22: This hill overlooking the Sea of Galilee was so quiet you could hear only the wind.
Simon and Andrew, James and John… one by one, the names were called.
Fishermen, a tax collector, a Zealot — people so different from one another became one group.
e23: When I saw the crowds, I sat down on this slope, and my disciples came to me.
Right here I told them, You are the salt of the earth and the light of the world.
Can you hear the wind brushing through the grass?
e24: A centurion in this town had a servant he valued, who was sick and dying.
Jewish elders came and pleaded with me, saying he had even built them their synagogue.
I never even crossed his doorstep, yet the servant was already well.
e25: In front of this town gate, I met the funeral procession of a widow's only son.
When I saw the mother weeping as she followed, my heart was deeply moved for her.
I touched the coffin and the bearers stood still — and I gave the son back to his mother.
e26: Simon the Pharisee invited me to a meal at his house in this town.
A woman known as a sinner came in with a jar of perfume and wept behind me at my feet.
As the fragrance filled the room, Simon watched without a word.
e27: People kept crowding in, so I got into a boat and sat on the water.
I began with the story of a sower, and one parable followed another.
Stand by the shore and listen. The water carries the sound far.
e28: As evening came we were crossing this lake, when a fierce storm swept over us.
While the waves broke into the boat, I was asleep in the stern on a cushion.
Even the voices of fishermen who had cast nets all their lives shook with fear.
e29: As soon as I got out of the boat, a man who lived among the tombs came running.
Not even chains could hold him; night and day he wandered among the tombs and hills, crying out.
The townspeople who came later saw him sitting there, dressed and in his right mind.
e30: Jairus, a leader of the synagogue, pushed through the crowd and fell at my feet.
On the way, a woman who had been ill for twelve years came up behind me and secretly touched my clothes.
In a room in his house lay a girl twelve years old.
e31: My disciples and I crossed by boat to this remote place, but the people got here first.
All there was: five barley loaves and two fish that one boy had.
It was spring, near the Passover, and the grass was green. The people sat on it in groups.
e32: I prayed on the mountain, while my disciples struggled against the wind in the middle of this lake.
In the fourth watch of the night, they saw me walking on the water and screamed, A ghost!
Peter walked a few steps, then saw the strong wind and began to sink.
e33: The crowd who had eaten the bread took boats the next day and came here looking for me.
They brought up the manna their ancestors ate in the wilderness.
A murmur spread through the synagogue, and from that day many disciples turned away.
e34: I left Galilee for this Gentile land in the north, hoping to stay without anyone knowing.
But a Greek woman heard about me, came and fell at my feet.
For her little daughter tormented by an unclean spirit, that mother would not give up.
e35: People brought me a man who was deaf and could hardly speak.
I took him aside, away from the crowd, to a quiet place.
His tongue was set free, and he began to speak plainly.
e36: This is at the foot of Mount Hermon, where the Jordan's waters spring up from under the rock.
My disciples and I had walked a long way north from Galilee to get here.
From here I began to tell my disciples about the suffering waiting for me in Jerusalem.
e37: I took only Peter, James and John and climbed this high mountain to pray.
While I prayed, Moses and Elijah appeared and talked with me.
Not knowing what he was saying, Peter blurted out that he would build three shelters.
e38: On the way back, my disciples argued in low voices about which of them was the greatest.
At the house, I stood a little child in the middle of them and took him in my arms.
Then Peter came and asked how many times he had to forgive his brother.
e39: At the Festival of Shelters, this city was full of pilgrims and huts woven from branches.
Early in the morning, people stood a woman caught in adultery in the middle of this courtyard.
Without answering, I bent down and wrote something on the ground with my finger.
e40: On the road, I noticed a man who had been blind from birth.
With mud on his eyes he came to this pool, and for the first time in his life he saw light.
However often they questioned him, he didn't back down — he told exactly what had happened.
e41: An expert in the law tried to test me by asking the way to eternal life.
I answered with a story about a man going down to Jericho and a Samaritan.
In this village Martha welcomed me, and Mary sat at my feet and listened.
e42: In winter, at the Festival of Dedication, I was walking in Solomon's Porch of this temple.
People surrounded me and pressed me: If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.
When they picked up stones again, I went away across the Jordan.
e43: Tax collectors and sinners gathered here one by one to listen to me.
The Pharisees muttered that I even ate with sinners.
So I told them three stories about finding what was lost — and never giving up until it was found.
e44: Lazarus had been in the tomb four days when I reached this village.
Martha came running out, and then Mary fell at my feet, weeping.
When I saw them weeping together, I wept too.
e45: People brought little children here for me to lay my hands on them.
My disciples scolded them, but I took the children in my arms and blessed them.
A man with great wealth went away sad, his face gloomy.
e46: By this dusty roadside sat blind Bartimaeus, begging.
The more people told him to be quiet, the louder he called to me.
Zacchaeus, the short chief tax collector, climbed a sycamore tree to see me.
e47: Six days before the Passover, at a supper in this village, Lazarus — alive again — sat with us.
Mary came in holding a jar of nard and poured it on my head and feet.
The rich fragrance filled the whole house, and no one dared speak first.
e48: I rode down this slope on a young donkey no one had ever ridden.
Pilgrims spread their cloaks on the road, came out with palm branches and shouted.
When the road turned and the city spread out before me, I looked at it and wept.
e49: On the way here I saw a fig tree full of leaves but with no fruit at all.
In this outer court I overturned the money changers' tables and the benches of those selling doves.
When the uproar died down, children shouted out loud in this courtyard.
e50: This courtyard was tense with sharp questions meant to trap me.
I had them bring me a denarius and asked whose face was stamped on it.
As I sat across from the offering box, a widow quietly put in two small coins.
e51: As we left the temple, one of my disciples looked up at the huge stone walls in wonder.
Toward sunset, I sat on this mountain facing the temple and talked with four disciples.
Look down at the city below. That day, too, the sun was setting like this.
e52: Peter and John prepared the Passover table in this upper room.
When evening came, I wrapped a towel around my waist and washed my disciples' feet one by one.
During the meal, Judas got up and went out. And it was night.
e53: The night after the supper, we crossed the Kidron Valley and came into this olive grove.
I fell to the ground a little way off and prayed, while my disciples, worn out, fell asleep.
When a crowd came with torches, the disciples all scattered and ran.
e54: With my hands bound, I was taken through the high priest's house, and at daybreak handed over here.
That night, when Peter in the courtyard denied knowing me the third time, the rooster crowed.
Pilate found no guilt in me, but in the end he handed me over to the shouting crowd.
e55: At nine in the morning, on this hill, I was nailed to the cross.
From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land.
At sunset, Joseph and Nicodemus laid me in a new tomb cut in the rock, in a garden.
e56: At dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene came and found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
Even after the disciples went home, she stood alone outside the tomb.
Her eyes were so blurred with tears that she thought I, standing behind her, was the gardener.
e57: That afternoon, two disciples were walking this road, talking in heavy voices.
I walked alongside them and explained what Moses and the prophets had written about me.
At the table, the moment I broke the bread and handed it to them, their eyes were opened.
e58: On the evening of the day of the resurrection, the disciples were gathered in this room with the doors locked.
They thought I was a ghost, so in front of them I ate a piece of broiled fish.
Eight days later, Thomas, who hadn't been there, met me in this room too.
e59: My disciples had cast empty nets all night, and at daybreak I waited for them on this shore.
Peter wrapped his outer garment around him and jumped straight into the water.
There were 153 large fish, and yet the net did not tear.
e60: The eleven disciples climbed this mountain I had told them about and waited for me in silence.
Among those who bowed down, some still doubted.
And to them, I came near. Feel the wind on the mountaintop.
e61: For forty days after I rose, I appeared to my disciples many times.
That day I led them out of the city, as far as near Bethany.
As I lifted my hands and blessed them, I was taken up into heaven.
